lines.text: Line two hundred nine, is finished, is checked after each execute.
Lines two hundred ten and eleven: a waypoint is done inside its switch radius, at least five centimeters.
Otherwise, lines two hundred thirteen to sixteen check all three. We're three meters away, so: false.
Lines two hundred nineteen to thirty-five: use corner rule. Let's trace our ninety degree route.
Two arrows. In: two, zero. Out: zero, one point five.
Line two hundred twenty-eight finds the turn between them, with the cross product and the dot product.
The cross product measures how much the arrows point across each other; the dot product, how much along.
Cross is three, dot is zero. A-tan-two of three and zero: ninety degrees.
Lines two hundred twenty-nine and thirty: forty percent of the shorter leg is zero point six, capped at zero point four.
Lines two hundred thirty-one to thirty-four: the turn is over one degree, so use the corner formula.
Six times zero point four, over one. Square root: one point five five meters per second.
The board's formula, in Java. Execute then brakes to it at the switch circle.
